newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Henan bans bank loans for villas, shares.
newsitem.headline: China's Henan bans bank loans for villas, shares.

text.p: China's central Henan province will strictly ban the use of bank loans to build luxury villas, office buildings and restaurants and buy shares in 1997, the China news service said on Wednesday.

The Henan branch of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, would implement a system to supervise the use of loans extended by local state-owned commercial banks this year, it quoted branch president Pei Qunguo as saying.
The province has set a target to withdraw 2.0 billion yuan ($240 million) of currency from circulation in 1997, Pei said.
Deposits in the province's financial institutions would rise by 20 percent this year and loans were expected to increase by 18 percent, he said.
The rate of bad loans should drop by 2-3 percentage points this year, he added.
